appraisal_events.evidence: Je ne crois pas que Robert se trompât absolument. Le dénigrement furieux était souvent chez Bloch l'effet d'une vive sympathie qu'il avait cru qu'on ne lui rendait pas... il a été d'une tendresse telle que je ne peux pas me montrer ingrat envers un tel ami.
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup's account of Bloch's wounded-affection-turned-tenderness is explicitly endorsed by the narrator, reframing Bloch's habitual prickliness as evidence of deep, loyal attachment.

appraisal_events.evidence: ma tante dit que c'est toi qui la fuis, que tu ne lui dis pas un mot. Elle se demande si tu n'as pas quelque chose contre elle.
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup relays his aunt's complaint that the narrator has been avoiding and ignoring her, a mild reproach that closes the passage.

status_effects.explanation: His earlier coldness is reinterpreted, with the narrator's own endorsement, as the flip side of genuine and lasting devotion.
He is quietly cast as having slighted Mme de Villeparisis, deflating the goodwill he had just extended toward Saint-Loup.

ambiguities: Saint-Loup's 'ma tante' is taken to refer to Mme de Villeparisis (his great-aunt, in whose salon the scene takes place); the passage does not name her explicitly at this point.
